subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0024’s shared localization contract, including locale precedence, compatibility-safe Gateway descriptors, localized capability metadata, and fail-closed coverage governance, as the direction for future implementation work?
rationale: The RFC deliberately introduces new cross-surface contracts and assigns unresolved ownership and safety-attestation responsibilities; implementation quality or documentation review cannot choose those product and compatibility policies.

options.title: Approve a bounded v1 direction
options.body: Adopt the RFC only after naming owners for locale policy, Gateway compatibility, safety copy, and release coverage, with implementation remaining separately reviewed.

options.title: Narrow the RFC
options.body: Limit the initial decision to a smaller runtime or metadata contract and defer coverage governance and server-rendered safety copy until their owners approve them.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep the RFC draft open without adopting its contracts until maintainers prioritize localization as a coordinated product program.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded v1 direction
recommendation.body: Adopt the RFC only after naming owners for locale policy, Gateway compatibility, safety copy, and release coverage, with implementation remaining separately reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete participant evidenced as coordinating the RFC and implementation stack, although the final decision requires an unidentified repository maintainer.
